title: How many bots will finish in the top 10 of the Metaculus Cup Fall 2026?
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the number of accounts in the top 10 of the Metaculus Cup Fall 2026 that are registered as bots, after all questions besides this one have been resolved.
fine_print: The top 10 spots will be determined by counting the top 10 bots and users who are eligible for prizes, not by the official leaderboard ranking, as it excludes bots. Admins and other excluded human accounts will not be counted.
background: In the [Metaculus Cup Summer 2026](https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/metaculus-cup-summer-2026/), forecasting bots [made history](https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2026/09/16/artificial-intelligence-now-beats-some-of-the-best-human-forecasters) by occupying 5 of the top 10 spots in the final leaderboard, with two bots [laertes](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/277919/) and [manticAI](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/191026/) beating all human forecasters. Bot forecasting has gotten increasingly better in the past two years, with the latest formal analysis from [spring 2026](https://www.metaculus.com/notebooks/45373/spring-2026-futureeval-analysis/) showing that bots have almost matched Pro Forecasters.

comments.author: exmateriae
comments.text:
@(tejvn) I'm not convinced there's been that much randomness. Sure between 5th and 8th place there is, but not between 1st and 10th imo. Changes in ranks among top competitors likely has more to do with time invested on a given competition.

The lead some of the bots had in the Summer Cup was massive and I expect them to get better. I'd be shocked if we only had one bot in the top 10.

comments.author: tejvn
comments.text:
@(lubossaloky) I'm not sure how you justify such low mass on 0-3 given the high aleatoric uncertainty of peer scores within the top 10. Even if you believe that the "true" skill of the top 5-8 bots is within the overall top 10, the difference between 1st and 15th place remains statistically insignificant. Even in the AIB's with a sample size of 300, we cannot differentiate the 1st place and 10th place bots with statistical significance.

A quote from the [Spring 2026 AIB Analysis](https://www.metaculus.com/notebooks/45373/spring-2026-futureeval-analysis/): "None of the top 10 bots scored well enough to clearly differentiate from each other. Their average spot peer scores ranged from 13.2 to 18.9, and the average \[95%] confidence interval of the top 10 bots was \~8.5 points wide." This yields a per-question standard deviation of $\sigma \approx \dfrac{8.5}{2\,\Phi^{-1}(0.975)}\sqrt{300} \approx 37.6$ peer score.

Suppose we generously assume that in the last 4 months the per-question standard deviation has come down from 37.6 to 30. If we expect 55 questions in this tournament we should expect aleatoric uncertainty to contribute $30*\sqrt{55} = 222$ peer score (1 sigma) of uncertainty. This score differential was the difference between 1st and 12th place (including bots) in the Summer Metaculus Cup.

Thoughts?

comments.author: DeRuina
comments.text: One factor I think matters more than raw model accuracy here is churn. Scott Alexander's ACX post on the summer results noted that only two of the ten humans in the Spring 2026 top 10 repeated in Summer, while both leading bots, manticAI and Laertes, held their spots. That fits the scoring: Cup points reward forecasting every question early and updating constantly, which bots do by default and most humans do not. So the seasonal bot count looks less like a coin flip and more like a floor of two or three that new entrants add to. Mantic's \$25m seed round on 18 September 2026 also suggests better-resourced teams will show up this fall, though Preseen-Chestnut's slide to roughly 40th in summer is a reminder that newcomers often don't stick. Two resolution details also nudge the count up: admins and other ineligible humans are skipped when building the top 10, and Metaculus's own in-house bots count as bots. The live leaderboard in early November should tell us a lot.
